items.title: Verstappen takes Red Bull's first pole of 2026 as Mercedes endure their worst qualifying of the year
items.summary: Max Verstappen led Q1, Q2 and Q3 and took pole with a 1m 35.130s, 0.298s clear of Lewis Hamilton, so Ferrari share the front row; Isack Hadjar was third on the road. The Race reports it is the first non-Mercedes-powered pole of the season and that Mercedes had their worst qualifying of 2026 despite debuting upgrades.
items.why_it_matters: Mercedes' upgraded package did not translate into one-lap pace at a track last visited in 2017, so Sunday's order is less predictable. Official classification (FIA provisional document) was still being processed when this was written; check it for the final grid.

sources.label: The Race: Verstappen takes first Red Bull pole of 2026

items.title: Hadjar, Lindblad and Colapinto carry grid penalties into Sunday's race
items.summary: Formula1.com reports Hadjar, Lindblad and Colapinto took penalties for exceeding power-unit components; Hadjar's is five places for a seventh ICE, and The Race's post-qualifying grid piece counts three penalties. Colapinto's five-place carry-over sanction is established by FIA Azerbaijan Document 66.
items.why_it_matters: Hadjar qualified on the Red Bull front-row side of the order, so his penalty reshuffles the top of the race grid. Use the official starting grid, not qualifying order.

items.title: Qualifying lap times deleted for Bearman, Antonelli and Gasly
items.summary: FIA Document 36 deletes lap times for Oliver Bearman, Kimi Antonelli and Pierre Gasly under Article 12.4.1.e because they did not use the track at turns 6 and 15. A separate summons for car 18 (alleged failure to follow Race Director's instructions, SC2-SC1 time) is listed; its outcome was not reviewed.
items.why_it_matters: Deleted laps can change who progressed or where they start. Check the provisional classification for each affected driver.

items.title: FIA confirms 14 upgrade items, including Mercedes' seven-part package
items.summary: FIA Document 12, issued Friday at 10:03 MYT, lists seven Mercedes items, two Racing Bulls items and one each for McLaren, Red Bull, Ferrari, Haas and Alpine. Williams, Aston Martin, Audi and Cadillac explicitly submitted no updates.
items.why_it_matters: All eleven teams now have reviewed declarations and inline readers on the Upgrades page. Counts refer to declared component rows, not lap-time gain or a guarantee that both cars ran every item.

sources.label: Formula1.com: Russell on Mercedes' Bahrain upgrades

items.title: FIA declares a Heat Hazard for Sunday's race
items.summary: FIA Document 3 declares a Heat Hazard under Article B1.5.10 because the official forecast Heat Index exceeds 31.0 degrees Celsius at some point during the Race. The venue is Sepang, with Sunday's start at 15:00 MYT / 10:00 Tallinn.
items.why_it_matters: This is an official declaration, not a generic weather warning. Do not equate Heat Index with ambient temperature or infer cooling-system requirements from temperature alone.
